Every mod Rimrooms was built alongside, what each one is for, and what you lose by skipping it.

The mod list

Rimrooms was built alongside 296 mods and expansions. This page says what each one is for, and what changes if you leave it out.

The base game is listed too, for context. It is not counted in that 296.

This whole page is the recommended list. Every mod on it was part of the profile Rimrooms was built in. The tag says what each one adds, not whether to install it.

It runs on vanilla, with no expansions

Rimrooms declares no mod as a hard dependency, and every game definition it names exists in the base game alone. That is checked on every build rather than assumed — a definition that needed an expansion would fail it.

So Required below means the game itself. Nothing on this page is required to launch, and everything else is capability you are adding on top.

TagHow manyWhat it means
Required2The game itself, and the mod this list is about.
Recommended2Gives Rimrooms a capability the base game cannot. Still not required.
Optional273Added capability. Rimrooms works the same with it or without it.
Visual only4Changes how things look and nothing else.
Not needed16Rimrooms does not interact with it. It is listed because it was in the profile, not as advice to skip it.

What Recommended means here

That the mod gives Rimrooms something the base game cannot. Not that it is popular, and not that a review of it went well.

An earlier version of this page derived the tag from how far each review had got, and recommended 83 mods including an animal sarcophagus. That was wrong and it is the reason this definition is written down.
